newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MARSEILLE FACE CRISIS OF CONFIDENCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARSEILLE FACE CRISIS OF CONFIDENCE.

text.p: Marseille, who in 1994 were relegated over a match-rigging scandal, have stumbled into a new crisis -- a lack of spirit undreamt of in those heady days under Bernard Tapie.

"I was ashamed. I saw players who did not deserve to wear the OM (Olympique Marseille) jersey," said the club's sporting director Marcel Dib after a shock 1-0 defeat at the weekend to Caen, who had not won in their previous 11 games.
"It's a delicate situation," said midfielder Eric Roy after a meeting on Sunday between management and players.

Angry fans pelted police with stones outside the Velodrome ground, scene of such recent glory days for the former European champions, as they vented their frustration. They were dispersed with tear gas after some officers were hurt.

Marseille's acting president Jean-Michel Roussier said: "I told them (the players) I could not tolerate attitudes which I did not think compatible with the jersey they wear and the profession they practice."
Roussier warned the players there would be sanctions if they did not observe two essential factors, respect for the jersey and the club and taking on their responsibilities.
"From the moment we explained our position on those two points, we expect progress," he added.
The fans have in particular criticised striker and captain Xavier Gravelaine and France midfielder Reynald Pedros, signed from Nantes in the off-season, for not pulling their weight.
Both players have criticed team mates' lack of technique.

"This (crisis) was just around the corner. We quickly become vulnerable if we don't manage to score. The defeat is collective and so are our doubts," said Gravelaine, also a newcomer signed this year.

Ireland striker Tony Cascarino, a veteran of Marseille's promotion side, complained that despite scoring for his country -- he hit two against Macedonia last week -- his club do not appear to have confidence in him.
"I don't understand why I was taken off at halftime. I finished as (club) top scorer last year, I score with my national team and I'm refused a chance at Marseille," he said.
"I've never known such a situation with players criticising their own team mates in the newspapers.
"This team is lacking in character. It's undoubtedly better than last year but it drops its arms too easily when things don't work out," Cascarino added.
"The defeat would not be that serious if we'd shown a real desire to win. Unfortunately, this was not the case on Saturday," said coach Gerard Gili.
But Gili dismissed talk of a crisis. "Without looking for excuses, OM have been unlucky with one absence after another (through injury or suspension) since the start of the season."
